Community Context and Scope of Work Palm Beach County (PBC), Florida, is home to nearly 1.5 million residents living in approximately 706,000 housing units.1 Although PBC is relatively affluent, more than 11% of its population is classified as low-income.2 Several census tracts across PBC are classified as disadvantaged due to high home and transportation energy burden,3 and having environmental justice considerations including exposure to legacy pollutants.4 All residents are exposed to extreme heat and many coastal and low-lying areas are at risk of flooding and sea level rise. A 2021 study by the Florida International University’s Metropolitan Center found that 56.6% of renters in Palm Beach County are cost-burdened, meaning they pay more than 30% of their income on housing.5 In addition, PBC has 107 identified disadvantaged communities under the Justice40 Initiative, including 23 along the Atlantic Ocean and Intracoastal Waterway and eight (8) along Lake Okeechobee. These communities include some of PBC’s most vulnerable populations to climate change and sea level rise, making it increasingly important to invest in resources for future resiliency. Renters in PBC face high housing costs and rely on landlords and building owners to make energy and water conservation investment decisions. Utility costs add to the lack of affordability in housing. The PBC Office of Resilience (OOR) and municipalities composing the Municipal Resilience Partnership (MRP) would like to develop a program to work with rental property owners and managers to make energy efficiency investments in their properties, passing utility cost savings to their tenants. MRP, through PBC OOR, applied to E2C Expert Match for analysis to justify and prioritize investment of potential weatherization and energy efficiency programs and policies to reduce energy costs for renters. However, they lack a building inventory that characterizes the makeup of housing units, their occupants, and their energy consumption to inform those decisions.
